# What Google API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy,
# which no real credential is. That run is thirty-five characters and so is a
# whole key body. It is spelled in lowercase because base64url holds the letters
# of both cases, so either spelling is a body; the case further down carrying a
# hyphen and an underscore is the rest of that alphabet, and Google's own
# example key carries all four together.

patterns: google-api-key

# The one prefix Google has ever shown a key written with. There is a single
# kind of string here rather than a table of them, as the GitLab and Slack files
# have: one key serves every Google API that takes a key rather than a
# credentialled principal, so nothing in the value says which API it was made
# for, and the four cases below are that one shape in four places.

case: an api key in an environment assignment
in:   GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  GOOGLE_API_KEY=«google-api-key»

case: an api key in the query string a request carries it in
in:   https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Tokyo&key=AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Tokyo&key=«google-api-key»

case: an api key in a client side configuration object
in:   {"apiKey":"AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy","projectId":"example"}
out:  {"apiKey":"«google-api-key»","projectId":"example"}

case: an api key on a command line
in:   gcloud services api-keys create --display-name=maps --key-string=AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  gcloud services api-keys create --display-name=maps --key-string=«google-api-key»

# The alphabet the thirty-five characters are written in. It is base64url, which
# is what every published statement of the shape admits and what Google's own
# example carries: that example holds both a hyphen and an underscore, so
# neither is inferred. The two characters standard base64 writes in their place,
# the plus and the slash, are not admitted, and a body carrying one is no key.

case: a body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:   AIza0123456789abcdef-hijklmnopqrstuvwx_
out:  «google-api-key»

case: a body carrying the two characters standard base64 uses instead
in:   AIza0123456789abcdef+hijklmnopqrstuvwx/
out:  AIza0123456789abcdef+hijklmnopqrstuvwx/

# The lengths either side of thirty-nine. Google states no length for an API key
# anywhere the pattern's author could find; what it states is that the string is
# encrypted, beside one example. Thirty-nine is what that example is and what
# every key published anywhere else is. Like the AWS access key ID and unlike
# the GitHub bodies, it is used as a count rather than a floor: thirty-eight
# characters are not a key, and forty are a key and one character that belongs
# to no credential. The second of those is the price of having no boundary
# behind the match — a boundary there would drop this key rather than trim it,
# and a real key written against a letter would come through whole.

case: a body of thirty-five characters is a key
in:   AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  «google-api-key»

case: a body of thirty-four characters is not
in:   AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx
out:  AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx

case: an alphabet run longer than a key is a key and what follows it
in:   AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:  «google-api-key»z

# What a key may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a key keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case: an api key after an underscore
in:   GOOGLE_API_KEY_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  GOOGLE_API_KEY_«google-api-key»

case: an api key after a letter
in:   xAIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  x«google-api-key»

# Two keys written together. The prefix is written in the alphabet a body is, so
# a key can begin inside the span of the one before it; the two spans overlap
# and are redacted as one. Written without that overlap the two are separate
# values, and both go.

case: a key beginning inside the key before it
in:   AIzaAIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  «google-api-key»

case: two keys with nothing between them
in:   AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyAIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  «google-api-key»«google-api-key»

# What is written after a key. The count is what ends one, so what follows it
# stays in the text whether or not it belongs to the alphabet a body is read in,
# and a dot, a full stop and a hyphen come to the same thing here.

case: an api key before a host name
in:   host=AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy.example.com
out:  host=«google-api-key».example.com

case: an api key at the end of a sentence
in:   the key is AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy.
out:  the key is «google-api-key».

case: an api key before a hyphenated word
in:   AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy-suffix
out:  «google-api-key»-suffix

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix is four characters of
# an alphabet of sixty-four, so a base64 value long enough carries it about once
# in seventeen million characters, and where the thirty-five behind it are in
# the alphabet too, those thirty-nine are redacted whether or not Google issued
# them. That is the answer rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a
# key's format exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing
# these would spare a real key written the same way. What is taken is
# thirty-nine characters of a value that was already opaque, which is what makes
# it admissible where the same reasoning would not carry a word of prose. The
# pattern's own file weighs the tightening that was available and what it would
# have cost.

case: the prefix inside a longer run of the alphabet
in:   payload=zzzzAIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzzz
out:  payload=zzzz«google-api-key»zzzz

case: the prefix where a signature stands
in:   eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.«google-api-key»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, which is
# read in the case Google writes it and in all four of its characters; the two
# after them are the count and the alphabet again, from the shortest run there
# is and from a body a space has broken. The last three carry no prefix at all,
# and could not: two of the prefix's four characters, the I and the z, are no
# hexadecimal digit, and no word is spelled with a capital I behind a capital A,
# so neither a digest nor prose holds a position to be found at however long it
# runs.

case: a lowercase prefix
in:   aiza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  aiza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case: an uppercase prefix
in:   AIZA0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  AIZA0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case: three characters of the prefix
in:   AIzb0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  AIzb0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case: the prefix alone
in:   AIza
out:  AIza

case: a body broken by a space
in:   AIza0123456789abcdef hijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:  AIza0123456789abcdef hijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case: a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:   0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABC
out:  0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABC

case: a hexadecimal digest
in:   sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:  sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case: prose
in:   there is no credential in this sentence
out:  there is no credential in this sentence

# And a Google credential this pattern has nothing to say about. A service
# account key is a JSON document holding an RSA private key, and the secret in
# it is the PEM block rather than any string with a prefix — there is no run of
# characters shaped like a key to find, so the document comes through whole and
# is a credential still to whoever reads it.

case: a service account key file
in:   {"type":"service_account","project_id":"example","private_key":"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n0123456789abcdef\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"}
out:  {"type":"service_account","project_id":"example","private_key":"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n0123456789abcdef\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"}
